correctness.rationale: The exact Hilbert pairwise-variance identity gives (r-1)A+rB<=(r-1)/2 and intracluster A<=(m-1)t²/(2m). Orthogonal regular-simplex Gram constructions realize both branches and establish nonexpansiveness. The nonnegative cross-distance deficit forces every plateau maximizer to have common centroid and all cross distances 1; r>=3 then forces each class norm²=1/2 and pairwise class orthogonality. Equality in the other branch forces all within and cross distances saturated. Centered Gram ranks prove required dimensions, and the sphere zero-sum parity argument at t=2 proves the minimal dimension law. Replayed exact-rational checker: 288 witness parameters, 1200 feasible sample maps, Gram-rank transition checks. Finite tests are corroboration only; analytic argument covers all integer r,m and real t in range. No unresolved critical lemma or infinite extrapolation.

value.rationale: The exact Lipschitz-to-centered-Hilbert-L² norm for an infinite, natural two-distance metric family is a meaningful invariant: it quantifies the maximum dispersion of nonexpansive Euclidean embeddings. An r-independent critical distance separates an isometric phase from a saturation phase; every norming map is classified, with a rank collapse by r-1 at the phase boundary and a sharp m-parity law for least Euclidean target dimension at t=2. These structural and dimension results go beyond the pre-existing two-class distortion threshold and real-scalar facet calculations, and can inform finite-distance embedding and semidefinite relaxation problems.
